elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 7.2 reads: "Customer has no obligation to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the terms Customer offers any other technology supplier." The affirmative MFN covenant is deleted and replaced with an express negative confirmation, which is reinforced by retained Section 12.3 ("Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment"). No other MFN mechanic runs against Customer in the cited text.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no Customer MFN obligation survives (7.2 is now an express disclaimer), so there is no MFN scope to limit to a defined product. The preferred outcome subsumes this fallback limit.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Customer MFN obligation remains in operative Section 7.2, so no duration cap is needed; the open-ended term that triggered the concern was removed rather than time-limited.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the Customer-side MFN deleted there is no comparison mechanic requiring like-for-like carve-outs.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: operative Section 7.2 no longer imposes any obligation on Customer to match or extend best third-party terms to Vendor, and the replacement sentence is an unconditional negative statement rather than a conditioned or deferred promise.
The fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because the Customer-side MFN has been eliminated entirely; scope, 12-month and like-for-like limits presuppose a surviving MFN obligation.

Minimality holds: only the single offending sentence in 7.2 was rewritten (obligation converted to an express no-obligation confirmation). No survival tail, procedure, expense language, or extra covenant was added, Vendor-favourable or unrelated language elsewhere was untouched, and Section 12.3 was retained verbatim. Retaining 7.2 as a confirmation rather than deleting it does not duplicate 12.3 in a harmful way, though outright deletion of 7.2 would have been equally acceptable; the residual overlap with 12.3's "no most-favoured-customer commitment" is a restatement of the same point and is the only mild redundancy, not an added operative requirement.

Intent is preserved: the edit creates no undefined term, no dangling cross-reference, and no contradiction \u2014 revised 7.2 now aligns with, rather than contradicts, retained Section 12.3. Pricing, payment and other commercial mechanics are unaffected.
No Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour existed in the cited text, so nothing beneficial to Customer was removed.
